title: Script editor, connected signal function, not scrolled into view
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: v4.7.dev2.official [778cf54da] v4.6.2.rc1.official [257ac3532] v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e] ### System information Godot v4.7.dev2 - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - GeForce GTX 550 Ti - Intel(R) Core(TM) i3-2100 CPU @ 3.10GHz (4 threads) - 11.95 GiB memory ### Issue description The connected signal function doesn't scroll into view, when a script has enough lines to fill the script editor window. ### Steps to reproduce - open the project: [signal-connected-func-not-scrolled-into-view.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26109611/signal-connected-func-not-scrolled-into-view.zip) - in the scene panel, select: `Node2D` - open the attached script: `node_2d.gd` - if your display resolution or scaling shows all 100 lines, add empty lines before the last line: `var last_line` to push it to the bottom of the script editor's window - click on the scripts first line to place the cursor there - in the signals panel, connect the signal: `visibility_changed()` to `Node2D` Issue: The signal function doesn't scroll into view. The script editor only scrolled down to the last line: `var last_line`. Even though the signal function has been added to the bottom of the script, and the cursor is blinking in the signal function. Expected: Scroll the signal function into view. The cursor is already blinking in it. This can be seen by scrolling down manually. A possible cause: Maybe it scrolls down to the scripts last line before adding the signal function. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [signal-connected-func-not-scrolled-into-view.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26109611/signal-connected-func-not-scrolled-into-view.zip)
